intro.author: Not named in the letter. Traditionally the apostle John; its style and vocabulary closely resemble John's Gospel. Some scholars attribute it to another leader in the same circle of churches.
intro.written: Probably about AD 85–95, traditionally from Ephesus
intro.audience: Believers in churches the writer knew well, probably in Asia Minor, whom he calls 'little children'
intro.setting: A group had recently left the fellowship ('They went out from us', 2:19) and were denying that Jesus Christ had 'come in the flesh' (4:2-3). Many scholars connect them with early teachings that treated the physical world as unimportant and denied that Christ truly had a human body. Those who remained were unsettled and needed assurance.
intro.purpose: The writer explains his aim: 'that ye may know that ye have eternal life' (5:13), giving tests of genuine faith: right belief about Jesus, obedience, and love for one another.
intro.bigIdea: God is light and God is love; those who truly know him walk in the light, love one another, and confess Jesus come in the flesh.

outline.title: Children of God love one another

commentary.t: THE FIRST GENERAL EPISTLE OF JOHN
